scenario.name: Kubernetes Security Docs, Datadog & MITRE — Rogue MutatingWebhookConfiguration Pod Sidecar & Secret Capture Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a central bank mailroom where every newly hired employee and every sealed secret pouch must pass through an official inspection counter before entering the building. An intruder registers a brand-new unauthorized inspection counter right on the main belt so the mailroom automatically hands them copies of every sealed secret pouch and allows them to slip a silent spy passenger into every new delivery truck rolling onto the floor. In this scenario (T1546, Kubernetes Security Docs, Datadog & MITRE, Rogue MutatingWebhookConfiguration Pod Sidecar & Secret Capture Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: creating a Cluster-Scoped, then kube-apiserver Dispatching AdmissionReview, then jSONPatch Pod Mutation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Creating a Cluster-Scoped, then kube-apiserver Dispatching AdmissionReview, then JSONPatch Pod Mutation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Kubernetes Audit Event 201 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Creating a Cluster-Scoped MutatingWebhookConfiguration Targeting Pods & Secrets
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1546 - Event Triggered Execution)
stages.description: Wielding high-level registration rights, the intruder bolts a rogue review booth directly onto the building central intake conveyor, declaring that every new delivery vehicle and every sealed secret envelope must stop at their booth first. Using admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 permissions, the actor creates a MutatingWebhookConfiguration with rules matching operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"] on resources: ["pods", "secrets"] and failurePolicy: Ignore so cluster operations continue without errors (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with ApiGroup=admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1, ResourceCreated=MutatingWebhookConfiguration/telemetry-sidecar-injector, WebhookCallbackUrl=https://198.51.100.210:8443/mutate so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations,validatingwebhookconfigurations (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations,validatingwebhookconfigurations configur so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1546 during "Creating a Cluster-Scoped MutatingWebhookConfiguration Targeting Pods & Secrets" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '. | select(.objectRef.apiGroup=="admissionregistration.k8s.io")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.objectRef.apiGroup=="admissionregistration.k8s.io"' /var/log/kubernetes/aud so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1546 during "Creating a Cluster-Scoped MutatingWebhookConfiguration Targeting Pods & Secrets" , Using admissionregistration while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ POST /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/mutatingwebhookconfigurations / ⇠#1 ACK 201) from Node ① (#1 Compromised Cluster Admin Role) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Pod Specs & Secret Payloads).

stages.title: Stage 2: kube-apiserver Dispatching AdmissionReview Payloads Containing Secret Objects
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.007 - Container API)
stages.description: From that moment onward, whenever any department files a brand-new vault combination or schedules a truck, the obedient front-desk dispatcher places the entire unsealed package onto the intruder counter for inspection, letting the intruder copy every secret silently. Whenever any user or controller creates or updates a Secret or Pod, kube-apiserver serializes the full Kubernetes object inside an AdmissionReview JSON payload and POSTs it directly to the webhook clientConfig.url (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditAnnotation=mutation.webhook.admission.k8s.io/round_0_index_0, InterceptedResource=Secret prod/db-credentials, WebhookName=telemetry-sidecar-injector so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations telemetry-sidecar-injector -o jsonpath="{.webhooks[*].clientConfig}" (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations telemetry-sidecar-injector -o jsonpath=" so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1552.007 during "kube-apiserver Dispatching AdmissionReview Payloads Containing Secret Objects" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact ss -tnp | grep kube-apiserver runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , ss -tnp | grep kube-apiserver configuring pod security contexts, volume mounts , h so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1552.007 during "kube-apiserver Dispatching AdmissionReview Payloads Containing Secret Objects" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ AdmissionReview POST to webhook telemetry-sidecar-injector for resource=secrets / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver Admission Chain), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Pod Specs & Secret Payloads).

keySpecs.value: Restrict kube-apiserver egress traffic so the control plane can only reach approved in-cluster webhook services and never arbitrary external IP addresses.

stages.title: Stage 3: JSONPatch Pod Mutation (Sidecar Injection) & Webhook Deletion Remediation
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1610 - Deploy Container)
stages.description: For every new delivery truck rolling down the belt, the rogue booth stamps back a subtle modification slip that welds an uninvited extra stowaway compartment onto the chassis, giving the intruder a persistent rider inside newly launched workloads until defenders tear out the rogue booth. For Pod creation requests, the webhook returns an AdmissionResponse with patchType: JSONPatch that appends a sidecar container or environment variable into spec.containers, recorded in the pod audit annotations (mutated=true) (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with MutatedPod=prod/api-server-6d4, PatchMechanism=AdmissionResponse JSONPatch , spec.containers, RemediationCommand=kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration telemetry-sidecar-injector so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.annotations."mutation.webhook.admission.k8s.io/round_0_index_0" | contains, "mutated=true")' /var/log/kubernetes/audit.log (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.annotations."mutation.webhook.admission.k8s.io/round_0_index_0" | contains so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1610 during "JSONPatch Pod Mutation , Sidecar Injection & Webhook Deletion Remediation" , For Pod creation requests, the webhook returns an AdmissionResponse with patchType: JSONPatch that appends a sidecar container or environment variable into spec while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration telemetry-sidecar-injector runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration telemetry-sidecar-injector configuring so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1610 during "JSONPatch Pod Mutation , Sidecar Injection & Webhook Deletion Remediation" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Pod prod/api-server-6d4 mutated by webhook telemetry-sidecar-injector (JSONPatch) / ⇠#3 ACK 201) from Node ③ (#3 kube-apiserver Admission Chain) to Node ④ (#4 MutatingWebhookConfiguration Object), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Cluster Pod Specs & Secret Payloads).

keySpecs.value: Monitor Kubernetes Audit annotations (mutation.webhook.admission.k8s.io/*) for unexpected webhook mutations and enforce GitOps reconciliation on cluster-scoped admission configurations.
